answer: Verifiable Effort Ledger. Each identity must periodically submit a solved compute task whose answer is checkable but whose work cannot be reused; nodes store the last accepted result as a relic proving continuity. A challenger can request recomputation, so faking history costs real machine-time. New identities start on a small knoll of low trust and can only harbor limited message throughput until the ledger lengthens. An attacker pays sustained parallel compute and loses accumulated work on any failed audit.
